title: Finite principal-cover descent for dg derived Hom
statement:
Let $S$ be a commutative ring and $C$ an associative unital dg $S$-algebra with central degree-zero $S$-action and $S$-linear differential. Use left dg module derived categories and signs of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization], applied to a point. Let $r\geq1$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in S$ generate the unit ideal. For $f\in S$ define $S_f$ and $M_f$ by inverting $1,f,f^2,\ldots$ in the ring and in each term of a module, respectively, and put $C_f=S_f\otimes_SC$. For nonempty $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ put $f_J=\prod_{j\in J}f_j$. Let $M,N\in D(C)$ be arbitrary, possibly unbounded.

Let $R\operatorname{Hom}_C(M,N)\in D(S)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] denote derived dg-linear Hom: choose a quasi-isomorphism $P\to M$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_C^\bullet(P,L)$ acyclic for every acyclic dg module $L$, and use $\operatorname{Hom}_C^\bullet(P,N)$, whose degree $q$ consists of graded $C$-linear maps of degree $q$, with $h(cx)=(-1)^{q|c|}c h(x)$ and differential $dh=d_Nh-(-1)^qhd_P$. This construction is independent up to its canonical derived isomorphism and has $H^qR\operatorname{Hom}_C(M,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(C)}(M,N[q])$.

Localization is exact and has the derived extension--restriction adjunction. The canonical maps induce a natural isomorphism in $D(S)$
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_C(M,N)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}\left[\prod_{|J|=1}R\operatorname{Hom}_{C_{f_J}}(M_{f_J},N_{f_J})\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_{C_{f_{\{1,\ldots,r\}}}}(M_{f_{\{1,\ldots,r\}}},N_{f_{\{1,\ldots,r\}}})\right].$$
All terms on the right are restricted to $S$. The finite alternating Cech direction has degree $p=|J|-1$ and total differential $\delta+(-1)^pd_{\mathrm{Hom}}$; its transition maps are induced by localization. The comparison is the augmentation into the singleton coordinates. No compactness, flatness or Noetherian hypothesis on $M,N,C,S$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08D2 (lemma-alternating-cech-complex-complex-computes-cohomology), finite affine Cech resolution; dg-Hom refinement obtained by applying Hom from a homotopically projective dg resolution to the finite localization resolution. This derived dg Hom statement is agent-formulated, not quoted verbatim from the tag.

proof.text: Pass from left $C$-modules to right modules over the graded opposite $C^{\mathrm{op}}$, with $a*b=(-1)^{|a||b|}ba$ and $x\cdot a=(-1)^{|x||a|}ax$. These formulas preserve the differential, quasi-isomorphisms and Hom complexes: for a degree-$q$ map, right linearity becomes $h(ax)=(-1)^{q|a|}ah(x)$. Right shifts with unchanged action become precisely the signed left shifts in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. Apply [lem-sfb-dg-property-p-resolution] over $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ and then [lem-sfb-dg-property-p-homotopically-projective]. Translating back gives a quasi-isomorphism $P\to M$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}_C^\bullet(P,L)$ is acyclic for every acyclic left dg module $L$. The $S$-action is retained: every graded $C$-linear map is $S$-linear because $S$ acts centrally in degree zero. Neither cited theorem requires boundedness or flatness.

For any homotopically projective $P$, [lem-sfb-dg-homotopically-projective-hom-derived], transported by step 1, identifies chain maps modulo homotopy from $P$ with maps in $D(C)$. Apply it also to $N[q]$: degree-zero chain maps $P\to N[q]$ are exactly closed degree-$q$ elements of the displayed Hom complex, and boundaries are homotopies, with the signed shift action. This gives $H^q\operatorname{Hom}_C^\bullet(P,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(C)}(M,N[q])$. For two such resolutions $P\to M$, $P'\to M$, lift their canonical derived comparison and its inverse using the same bijection. The composites represent identities, hence are homotopic to identities. Precomposition gives mutually inverse chain homotopy equivalences on Hom complexes; homotopic lifts induce the same map in $D(S)$. This proves the canonical independence of the chosen resolution and defines the contravariant functor on $M$. All maps and homotopies used are $S$-linear.

For $f\in S$, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] applied to cycles and boundaries shows $H^n(L_f)=H^n(L)_f$; thus localization preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Restriction keeps the underlying complex and is exact. Ordinary extension along $C\to C_f$ is localization: the mutually inverse balanced maps are $(c/s)\otimes x\mapsto cx/s$ and $x/s\mapsto(1/s)\otimes x$, where $s$ is a power of $f$. They commute with differentials because $ds=0$. Consequently this extension is already its derived functor. The extension--restriction adjunction of [lem-sfb-ringed-dg-scalar-adjunction], on a point and for left modules, is therefore the required exact derived localization adjunction, with its action counit.

source.place: Tag 00CS (proposition-localization-exact); dg scalar adjunction: sdga.tex Tags 0FTF (lemma-derived-tensor-product), 0FTR (lemma-derived-adjoint-push-pull)

proof.text: For any dg $C_f$-module $L$ there is an isomorphism of $S$-complexes $\operatorname{Hom}_{C_f}^\bullet(P_f,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_C^\bullet(P,\operatorname{Res}L)$. In every degree its forward map restricts along $x\mapsto x/1$, and its inverse sends $h$ to $x/s\mapsto s^{-1}h(x)$. Fractions are well defined since $s$ acts invertibly on $L$; the same formula verifies the signed $C_f$-linearity. The Hom differential commutes with this formula since $d(s)=0$. An acyclic $L$ remains acyclic under restriction, so the right complex is acyclic by the choice of $P$. Hence $P_f$ is homotopically projective, and step 3 shows $P_f\to M_f$ is a quasi-isomorphism. With $L=N_f$ the displayed complexes compute $R\operatorname{Hom}_{C_f}(M_f,N_f)$ and $R\operatorname{Hom}_C(M,\operatorname{Res}N_f)$, respectively. For further localization the formula remains $h(x/s)/t=h(x)/(st)$, so these identifications commute with the transition maps.

source.place: Tag 09KY (lemma-hom-derived); explicit fraction form of the extension--restriction Hom adjunction

proof.text: Put $B^{p,t}=\prod_{|J|=p+1}(N_{f_J})^t$ for $0\leq p<r$, zero otherwise. Its horizontal differential $\delta$ is the alternating sum of further localizations and its vertical differential is $d_N$; they commute. Form $T(N)^n=\bigoplus_{p=0}^{r-1}B^{p,n-p}$ with $D=\delta+(-1)^p d_N$. Give column $p$ the left action $c\star x=(-1)^{p|c|}cx$. Then $D^2=0$. For $|c|=a$, the $\delta$ terms in $D(c\star x)=d_Cc\star x+(-1)^ac\star D(x)$ agree because $(-1)^{pa}=(-1)^a(-1)^{(p+1)a}$; the internal terms agree by the original module Leibniz rule. Thus $T(N)$ is a dg $C$-module. The singleton localization maps define a dg map $u:N\to T(N)$: its horizontal differential is zero since on each pair the two localizations coincide, and column zero has unchanged differential and action.

source.place: Tag 08D2 (lemma-alternating-cech-complex-complex-computes-cohomology); explicit left-dg refinement and total signs

proof.text: For each integer $t$, apply [lem-pc-affine-cech-complex] to the $S$-module $N^t$ and to the unit-ideal family $f_1,\ldots,f_r$. It gives exactness of $0\to N^t\to B^{0,t}\to\cdots\to B^{r-1,t}\to0$. Equivalently the singleton map from $N^t[0]$ to this horizontal row is a quasi-isomorphism: its degree-zero kernel is the image of $N^t$, this map is injective, and all positive row cohomology vanishes. Apply [lem-sc-finite-strip-row-augmentation] in $S$-modules to the commuting double complex $B$, with $A=N$, width $r$, and the maps just described. Its hypotheses hold in every integer degree, and its specified augmentation is exactly $u$. It follows that the underlying $S$-complex map $u:N\to T(N)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The width is finite even when $N$ is unbounded.

source.place: Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), variant in the other variable and finite horizontal strip; standard affine alternating Cech exactness

proof.text: The cone of $u$ is acyclic by [lem-sfb-dg-homotopy-acyclic-localization], transported to left modules as in step 1. Homotopical projectivity therefore makes $\operatorname{Hom}_C^\bullet(P,\operatorname{Cone}(u))$ acyclic. Splitting a map to the cone into its two components identifies this complex with $\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{Hom}_C^\bullet(P,u))$: on a degree-$q$ pair $(a,b)$ the differential is $(d a+u b,-d b)$, using the signed shifted action. The same cone criterion, applied to the dg algebra $S$ concentrated in degree zero, shows that $\operatorname{Hom}_C^\bullet(P,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_C^\bullet(P,T(N))$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This uses Hom on an acyclic cone, rather than exactness of ordinary Hom on the Cech rows.

source.place: Tag 09KW (lemma-acyclic), cone criterion; the Hom-cone component calculation uses the displayed Hom differential

proof.text: A degree-$q$ map $P\to T(N)$ is uniquely its finite family of components $h_{p,J}:P^i\to (N_{f_J})^{i+q-p}$. Signed $C$-linearity in $T(N)$ reads $h_{p,J}(cx)=(-1)^{(q+p)|c|}ch_{p,J}(x)$, which is exactly degree-$(q-p)$ linearity into $N_{f_J}$. Conversely these components reconstruct the map by the finite sum of column inclusions. This remains true for an unbounded $P$: an arbitrary family indexed by $i$ can be regrouped across the fixed finite set of pairs $(p,J)$. In these coordinates the Hom differential is $\delta h_{p-1}+(-1)^p d_Nh_p-(-1)^q h_p d_P=\delta h_{p-1}+(-1)^p(d_Nh_p-(-1)^{q-p}h_pd_P)$. Thus there is an actual isomorphism of $S$-complexes $\operatorname{Hom}_C^\bullet(P,T(N))\cong\operatorname{Tot}[\prod_{|J|=p+1}\operatorname{Hom}_C^\bullet(P,N_{f_J})]$ with exactly the differential in the statement.

source.place: Tag 08D2; finite regrouping and the explicit Hom-total differential computation

proof.text: Combine steps 7 and 8, then apply step 4 to every $f_J$. Each local complex becomes $\operatorname{Hom}_{C_{f_J}}^\bullet(P_{f_J},N_{f_J})$, a representative of the required derived Hom. The isomorphisms of step 4 commute with all further localizations, so they identify the whole finite diagram, not just its individual objects. This gives the asserted isomorphism in $D(S)$. The degree-zero-column component sends $h$ to $x/s\mapsto h(x)/s$ in each singleton, and all higher column components are zero; hence the comparison is the stated augmentation. These strict models also specify the total of the derived diagram. A map of target modules commutes with each fraction map and with $\delta$. A map of source modules is represented by a map between their projective resolutions using step 2; precomposition commutes with every displayed construction. Changing such a lift by a homotopy changes the resulting maps by a homotopy. The same holds for a change of projective resolution. Therefore the comparison is natural in both derived variables and independent of choices. For $r=1$, $f_1$ is a unit and this is the identity under localization; zero localizations or zero modules simply give zero coordinates. No argument used any finiteness, boundedness, flatness or Noetherian condition beyond the finite unit-ideal cover.
